To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
not all vasorelaxants lower cytosolic free Ca2+ levels.
not all vasorelaxants lower cytoplasmic calcium levels in smooth muscles and that vasorelaxant effects of agents that increase cAMP levels are not mediated by lowering of cytoplamic calcium levels.
the vasodilators isoprenaline, forskolin and papaverine cause relaxation of ferret portal smooth muscle without decreasing cytoplasm Ca2+ levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cytoplasm calcium in the regulation of smooth muscle tone.
the mechanisms of action of the vasodilator drugs, sodium nitropruside and papaverine, and with the role of cyclic AMP in the regulation of smooth muscle contractility.
the mechanisms of vasodilator action in vascular smooth muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in intact smooth muscle, the relationship between cytoplasmic calcium levels and force is not a simple one.
the action of a vasodilator is to cause a decrease in cytoplasm calcium levels in only a small percentage of cases.
, while the lowering of cytoplamic Ca2+ levels may be an important mechanism for the action of some vasodilators, it is not an absolute requirement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of cyclic AMP on force and light are not necessarily related.
, in the intact cell, calcium‐force relations are not necessarily a simple reflection of the changes in cytoplasm calcium.
vasodilators that cause a decrease in force by increasing cyclic AMP levels in smooth muscle can do so by more than just reducing cytoplasmic calcium levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
not all vasorelaxants cause a lowering of intracellular Ca2+, and that some vasorelaxation may be due to an uncoupling or inhibition of calcium‐sensitivity of the smooth muscle.
the calcium‐force relation can be uncoupled in intact cells by agents associated with an increase in cytosolic cyclic AMP.
not all vasorelaxants decrease cytoplasmic calcium levels.
